summary.title: Don't Call Yourself A Programmer, And Other Career Advice
summary.one_liner: Software engineers advance their careers by understanding business value (raising revenue or cutting costs), networking, and negotiating, rather than by chasing specific languages or stacks.
keywords: does programming language matter for career

college degree gpa importance for jobs
takeaways: Frame your value in terms of business outcomes (revenue added or costs reduced) rather than in terms of a programming identity or tech stack.
Most hiring happens through personal introductions and networking, so meeting people in person and helping others matters.
Salary is one lever among many; negotiate after agreement in principle, and research salary ranges via people at the company.
Treat startup equity skeptically; overestimate of success and of your share is common.
GPA, major, and academic credentials matter much less in industry than engineers often assume.
summary.summary: This essay by Patrick McKenzie is a informal career guide for young engineers, aimed at closing gaps between what universities teach and how the software industry works. It argues that most software is internal line-of-business work judged by its effect on revenue and costs, and that engineers are usually cost centers. It then covers advice on job identity, networking and informal hiring, academia versus industry, salary negotiation, valuing equity grants, and whether to join a startup. The approach is opinionated anecdote and rules of thumb drawn from the author's own experience rather than data.
